clue.text: Cease association with component firm

parts.note: a component is a part of a larger whole
a firm is a business, a company

explanation.surface: A business statement that one firm is cutting ties with a component maker.
explanation.definitionFit: To part company is the idiom for separating and ending a relationship.

clue.text: Gather it's the cry of a self-confessed moron

definitions.text: the cry of a self-confessed moron

explanation.surface: Collect what an admitted fool shouts.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is 'I am a(n) ass' cut down to AM ASS: an ass is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate or collect; and an admitted idiot might say 'am ass'.

clue.text: Negotiated to be patiently dealt with

explanation.surface: Something was negotiated so as to be handled patiently.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties who negotiate are said to treat; someone given medical care as a patient has been seen to by a doctor.

clue.text: Bully for daughter gaining a university place

parts.note: a bull is an ox, a bovine animal
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Good for the daughter who's won a place at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully for' looks like the exclamation 'good for'; Bully is the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A city famous for its ancient university.

clue.text: Agreeable lake in rustic surroundings

indicators.note: the lake's letter sits inside the rustic person
the rustic word forms surroundings, enclosing the lake's letter

parts.note: a rustic is a country person, a peasant
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A pleasant lake set in country scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nice and enjoyable is agreeable.

clue.text: Itinerant sees cross depicted in restored icon

indicators.note: shown within, so the angry word sits inside the reworked icon
restoring an icon here means rebuilding its letters in a new order

parts.note: cross means angry, mad

explanation.surface: A wanderer sees a cross shown in a newly restored religious icon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' turns ICON into NOIC, and 'depicted in' places MAD inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering from place to place without settling is the travelling life of herders.

clue.text: Bungle commission to convert property for service accommodation

definitions.text: commission to convert property for service accommodation

explanation.surface: Mess up a contract to turn a building into barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: A mess is where service personnel eat; to 'make a mess of it' reads as converting 'it', the property, into one.
explanation.definitionFit: To botch a task is to bungle it; turning a property into a services' dining hall also fits.

clue.text: Look into getting away with a slice of meat

indicators.note: the word for look goes into the word for getting away

parts.note: an escape is a getaway
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Investigate running off with a cutlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin boneless cut of meat, beaten flat, such as veal.

clue.text: Where becalmed sailors become depressed

explanation.surface: Windless seamen grow gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: The doldrums are equatorial calm zones where sailing ships stalled; being there also means low in spirits.

clue.text: Humble headquarters

explanation.surface: A modest head office.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase is to humble or degrade; headquarters can be called a base, read here as 'a base'.

clue.text: Member of an order whose stonework is priceless

definitions.text: Member of an order whose stonework is priceless

parts.words: Member of an order whose stonework is priceless
parts.note: a fraternal lodge member, read as a builder in stone whose work costs nothing

explanation.surface: A member of some religious order whose masonry is beyond value.
explanation.definitionFit: The fraternal order took its name from medieval stoneworkers; here the builder's work is taken as given away at no charge.

clue.text: Tick given for using a plain vocabulary

explanation.surface: A teacher's tick awarded for writing in simple words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' is British slang for credit, as in buying 'on tick'; hire-purchase deals advertise payment on gentle conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying on credit is buying with gentle repayment arrangements; plain vocabulary uses simple words.

clue.text: Made a threat involving loss of living

indicators.note: the letters sought are contained within the run of words 'Made a threat'

explanation.surface: Someone issued a threat that someone else would lose their livelihood.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying is the end, or loss, of life.

clue.text: Complaint by a female graduate

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate's degree
a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A grievance lodged by a woman with a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or ailment.

clue.text: See an object with feelings of disgust

parts.note: lo is an old interjection meaning see
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Viewing some item and feeling revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense hatred and revulsion are strong feelings of aversion.

clue.text: Agreeing on the best place to provide domestic electricity?

definitions.text: the best place to provide domestic electricity?

explanation.surface: Deciding together where to put the household power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as IN AC CORD: alternating current comes into the home along a flex.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of one accord means being in agreement; a power flex carrying alternating current is where mains supply runs.

clue.text: Salvationists give heart to less refined campaigner

indicators.note: the Salvationists' letters become the centre of the word for less refined

parts.note: cruder means coarser, less refined
SA is the Salvation Army

explanation.surface: Salvation Army members encourage a rougher activist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who campaigns vigorously for a cause, like a medieval holy warrior.

clue.text: Children require little fish

explanation.surface: Kids need tiny fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Young children are jokingly called this phrase; it also names fry, newly hatched fish.

clue.text: Bounty was a sizeable ship

parts.note: sizeable means large
SS is a steamship

explanation.surface: The Bounty was a big ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bounty was a famous ship, so the surface invites a naval reading; here it means generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous giving or a gift, like a handout, is also called bounty.

clue.text: Private transaction proves a trying experience

parts.note: OR, other ranks, covers private soldiers
a deal is a business transaction

explanation.surface: A confidential business arrangement turns out to be hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful test, a hard trial endured.

clue.text: Shelter given to oriental migrant

parts.note: a refuge is a place of shelter
E for eastern, oriental

explanation.surface: An Eastern migrant is given asylum.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fleeing their country to seek safety elsewhere is a displaced migrant.

clue.text: Venomous substance son extracted from French fish

indicators.note: taken out of the French word for fish

parts.note: poisson is French for fish
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Toxin removed by a son from a French fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxin is a substance that harms or kills.

clue.text: Additional article coated with gold

indicators.note: the word for the article is covered all round by the heraldic gold

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
the definite article

explanation.surface: An extra item that has been gilded.
explanation.definitionFit: Another, further or extra item is an additional one.

clue.text: Betray and defeat factory workers

parts.note: to shop is British slang for informing on someone
to floor an opponent is to knock them down, beat them

explanation.surface: Sell out and crush the workforce of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The production area of a factory, and by extension the workforce there as opposed to management.

clue.text: Derived from oil EC manufactured

indicators.note: being manufactured, the letters are rebuilt into a new form

explanation.surface: A product made from oil by the European Community.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleic acid is a fatty acid obtained from olive and other oils.

clue.text: Malicious references send union into a frenzy

indicators.note: being thrown into a frenzy suggests the letters are wildly jumbled

explanation.surface: Spiteful remarks whip a trade union into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Insinuations are sly, often spiteful hints about someone.

clue.text: Light reflected from a single amethyst

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of letters in 'single amethyst'

explanation.surface: The sparkle off one purple gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: A glint is a brief flash of light bouncing off a surface.

clue.text: Acerbity results from a lack of capital

parts.note: stringency is financial tightness, scarcity of money

explanation.surface: Bitterness comes from being short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbity is sharpness or harshness, a sour severity.
